skill.name: baoyu-danger-x-to-markdown
skill.description: Convert X posts, threads, and articles into Markdown with YAML front matter. The skill uses a consent-gated reverse-engineered X API, optional authentication cookies, and optional local media downloads.
skill.summary: Save X posts, threads, and articles as organized Markdown files with metadata and optional local media.
skill.author: jimliu

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by ordinary JavaScript template literals, regular expression methods, expected X endpoints, configuration reads, and Markdown file handling. The audit confirms a shell-command injection risk in the WSL path resolver, and it flags deliberate handling of X authentication cookies plus host-controlled media downloads as risks requiring user trust and tighter controls.

remediation.issue: The WSL path resolver interpolates a value into an execSync shell command.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell-based execSync calls with spawnSync or execFile using argument arrays. Validate the returned path before using it.

remediation.issue: Authentication cookies are collected from Chrome or environment variables and persisted in a local JSON file.
remediation.suggestion: Document the credential scope clearly, restrict cookie-file permissions, avoid logging token prefixes, and provide an opt-out that never persists cookies.

remediation.issue: Media localization fetches HTTPS URLs taken from Markdown content without a strict host allowlist.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only approved media hosts, reject loopback and private-network destinations after DNS resolution, and enforce size, timeout, and redirect limits.

semantic_findings.description: The WSL helper interpolates the value returned by the Windows USERPROFILE query into an execSync shell command. A crafted environment value could change shell parsing and execute an unintended command.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent X Authentication Cookies
semantic_findings.description: The skill obtains auth_token and related X cookies from environment variables or a Chrome session, then stores them in a local JSON file for later requests. Compromise of that file or process can expose the user account session.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited code reads authenticated browser cookies and writes the cookie map to disk. This behavior is explicit and central to authenticated X retrieval.

semantic_findings.title: Host-Controlled Media Downloads
semantic_findings.description: Media localization fetches HTTPS URLs taken from Markdown content and writes the response to local files. Untrusted X content can therefore cause requests to attacker-selected hosts unless destinations are allowlisted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The candidate URL is derived from document content and then fetched with redirects enabled. The feature is legitimate, but its destination boundary is broader than the documented X media hosts.

content.value_statement: Saving X posts and articles manually loses structure, metadata, and media references. This skill retrieves selected X content and organizes it as Markdown with YAML front matter and optional local media.
actual_capabilities: Convert X posts and threads into Markdown with YAML front matter.
Extract X Articles and preserve article text, links, tweets, and media references.
Resolve authenticated X content through environment cookies or a Chrome login session.
Save output using predictable user-selected directories and filenames.
Download supported images and videos into local folders when the user enables media localization.
limitations: The skill depends on a reverse-engineered X API that can change without notice.
Authenticated content requires valid X cookies and may trigger account restrictions.
Media localization can contact URLs embedded in content and should use trusted inputs.
Output formatting depends on the source content and may not preserve every X feature.

use_cases.title: Archive Research Threads
use_cases.description: Convert a research thread into a searchable Markdown note with its source URL, author metadata, and linked media.

use_cases.title: Save Articles for Writing
use_cases.description: Extract an X Article into an editable Markdown draft for citation, review, and later synthesis.

use_cases.title: Build a Personal Knowledge Base
use_cases.description: Store selected posts in a predictable folder structure so they can be indexed by local notes and documentation tools.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this X post to Markdown with YAML front matter: [paste the X URL]. Keep the original source link.

prompt_templates.title: Archive a Thread
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this X thread to Markdown: [paste the X URL]. Preserve the thread order, author details, source links, and media references.

prompt_templates.title: Extract an Article
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this X Article to a clean Markdown document: [paste the X Article URL]. Include YAML front matter, headings, links, embedded posts, and media references.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Local Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these X URLs into separate Markdown files: [paste URLs]. Use consistent metadata, organize files by author and post ID, and download media only after asking for confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage a repeatable archive workflow.

output_examples.input: An X thread URL about a software release.
output_examples.output: A Markdown file with the thread text in order, author metadata, the original source link, and referenced media links.

output_examples.input: An X Article URL with headings, links, and embedded posts.
output_examples.output: A structured Markdown article with YAML front matter, readable sections, preserved links, and embedded post references.

output_examples.input: A post URL with the local media option enabled.
output: A Markdown file with rewritten local media links.
Separate imgs and videos folders beside the Markdown file.

best_practices: Review the consent notice and use a dedicated X session for archival work.
Store cookies securely and enable media downloads only for trusted content.
Keep the generated source URL and metadata so archived notes remain traceable.
anti_patterns: Do not provide cookies from an account that should not be accessed.
Do not use media localization on untrusted content without network restrictions.
Do not treat the generated Markdown as a complete backup of every X feature.

faq.question: What does this skill convert?
faq.answer: It converts X posts, threads, and X Articles into Markdown with YAML front matter.

faq.question: Does it require an X login?
faq.answer: Authenticated X cookies are required for the main retrieval workflow. They can come from environment variables or a Chrome session.

faq.question: Where are files saved?
faq.answer: Files use the selected output path. Without one, the default structure is x-to-markdown followed by the author and post identifier.

faq.question: Can it download images and videos?
faq.answer: Yes. The optional media workflow downloads supported media into local imgs and videos folders and rewrites the Markdown links.

faq.question: Is the X API official?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses a reverse-engineered X API and displays a consent notice before conversion.

faq.question: Which AI tools support it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools when the required runtime is available.
